title: File the business tangible personal property (and machinery and tools) return
question: Does my business have to file a personal property return, and when?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit); the Director of Finance acts as commissioner of the revenue and treasurer
summary: Every business in Albemarle County must file a business tangible personal property return by May 1 each year, even if it owns no property. List the furniture, fixtures, computers, equipment and tools it had on January 1, by year acquired, at full original cost. Manufacturers and similar businesses report machinery and tools separately. File online at AlbemarleCountyTaxes.org, or send the County's form by email, mail, fax or drop-off. The taxed value is 25% of cost in the first year, falling to 10%; the 2026 rate is $4.28 per $100. Bills are due June 25 and December 5, with no proration. Filing late adds 10% of the tax or $10, whichever is greater. Disputes go to the Director of Finance, then the Tax Commissioner or circuit court.

steps.step: Work out whether the business must file
steps.who: Every person or entity conducting business in Albemarle County (owner, partner or officer)
steps.how: File if the business had any furniture, fixtures, office equipment, computers, cell phones, copiers, tools, shop equipment or machinery in the County on January 1, owned or rented. A business with no property still files a return every year saying so. The form asks how the business operates without assets, and personal items or phones used in the business count as reportable. Property is taxed where it is physically located on January 1. Highway-licensed vehicles are not reported on this return (see caveats).
steps.deadline: Status is fixed as of January 1 (the tax day); the return is due May 1

steps.step: Register the business with the Office of Revenue Administration and have the County account number ready
steps.who: Business owner, with the Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: A business new to the County registers with the Office of Revenue Administration and gets a business license, a separate process: a new business files its license application inside 30 days of starting business, and licenses are renewed each year by March 1 (Existing Businesses page). The return asks for the Albemarle County account number, the legal and trade names and the Albemarle location address. A separate return is needed for each location.

steps.step: List all business property held on January 1, by year acquired, at full original cost
steps.how: List furniture, fixtures, office equipment (computers, cell phones, copiers), tools, shop equipment and machinery: all property used or available for use in the business on January 1. Include fully depreciated and expensed items, including IRS section 179 deductions. Use the full cost, including sales and use tax, freight and installation, and do not deduct trade-in allowances. Group items by purchase year; the 2026 form runs from 2025 back to '2019 & Prior'. Leave out highway-licensed vehicles, daily rental property, airplanes and boats. Leave out application software (report only the software needed to operate the computer) and equipment that cost less than $25 and is not machinery and tools, merchants' capital or short-term rental property. Miscellaneous and incidental property costing less than $500 (not machinery and tools) may be reported as one aggregate estimate of its total cost instead of item by item.
steps.deadline: Property in the business's possession on January 1

steps.step: Report machinery and tools separately if the business is a manufacturer or similar
steps.who: Manufacturers, miners, dairies, radio or television broadcasters, dry cleaners and laundries; processors and re-processors
steps.how: Enter machinery and tools cost in column C of the return and other business property in column B. A processor or re-processor reports both. DMV-registered vehicles are taxed as vehicles, but under state law the other vehicles and delivery equipment of these businesses count as machinery and tools. State law caps the machinery and tools rate at the general tangible personal property rate; for 2026 both are $4.28 per $100. The County decides the classification; if unsure, ask for a written ruling (see escalation).

steps.step: Report equipment the business leases or rents from others
steps.who: The business using leased or rented equipment (lessee)
steps.how: In the return's Leased Equipment section, give each lessor's name and address, a description of the property, the lease number, the monthly rental cost and the lease begin and end dates. Do not include the cost of leased equipment in the totals.

steps.step: Complete and sign the return, with the itemized asset list attached
steps.how: File online, or use the County's 2026 return form (a fillable PDF). Enter cost totals by purchase year; the form lists the assessment ratio for each year and computes the assessed value as (B + C) x D. Attach an itemized list with purchase year, description and original cost; page 2 of the form has a blank list and a sample. Entries such as 'Same as last year' or 'See attached', and federal Form 762, are not accepted. Tick 'Amended Return' to correct a return already filed. An owner, partner or officer must sign and date the return; willfully signing a return you do not believe to be true and correct is a Class 1 misdemeanor (Va. Code § 58.1-11).

steps.who: Business, to the Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: File online at AlbemarleCountyTaxes.org/Business. Or send the completed form by email to tax@albemarle.org, by mail to 401 McIntire Road, Suite 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902, or by fax to 434-243-7906. You can also drop it off at the County Office Building on McIntire Road during business hours, or in a 'Payment' box in its parking lot. The County's pages state no fee for filing. If May 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, state law allows filing on the next business day (May 1, 2027 is a Saturday).
steps.deadline: May 1 each year (the 2026 return was due May 1, 2026)
steps.fee: No filing fee stated; filing late adds a penalty of 10% of the tax shown on the return, or $10 if that is more

steps.step: If machinery and tools will be idle, tell the County in writing by April 1
steps.who: Machinery and tools taxpayers (manufacturers and the other businesses listed in s4)
steps.how: Under state law, idle machinery and tools leave the machinery and tools class: they are taxable as capital under § 58.1-1101 (the state's intangible personal property classification), so the County does not tax them as machinery and tools. Idle means out of use on the tax day, with no reasonable prospect of returning to use that year, and either out of use continuously for at least a year before the tax day or identified in writing by April 1 as equipment you intend to withdraw from service by the next tax day. If equipment identified that way goes back into use, tell the County in writing by the next return due date, without extension. It is then taxed for the year it returned to use, with interest; with timely notice no penalty is charged. The County's pages do not describe this, so ask the Business & Personal Tax Unit where to send the notice.
steps.deadline: On or before April 1 (for withdrawal from service by the next January 1); notice of return to use by the next return due date, without extension
steps.quote: have been specifically identified in writing by the taxpayer to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official, on or before April 1 of such year, as machinery and tools that the taxpayer intends to withdraw from service not later than the next succeeding tax day

steps.step: The Director of Finance assesses the property and works out the tax
steps.who: Director of Finance (Department of Finance & Budget), acting as commissioner of the revenue
steps.how: The assessed value is a percentage of original cost, set by purchase year: 25% in the first year, then 22.5%, 20%, 17.5%, 15%, 12.5%, and 10% for the seventh year and older. The tax is the assessed value times the rate: $4.28 per $100 for 2026, a multiplier of 0.0428. For example, $10,000 of equipment bought in 2025 is assessed at $2,500, so the tax is $107. On request, the County must describe its valuation methods and take the condition of the property into account. For machinery and tools, on your written request it must also consider a bona fide, independent appraisal you present. If no return is filed, the Director of Finance makes a statutory assessment from the best information available, and the late filing penalty applies.

steps.step: Pay the tax bill in two halves, by June 25 and December 5
steps.who: Business owner, to the Department of Finance & Budget (Office of Revenue Administration)
steps.how: State law requires the County to mail the bill at least 14 days before the due date. Pay online at AlbemarleCountyTaxes.org: e-checks are free, and cards carry a fee of 2.50% (credit) or 2.35% (debit), at least $1.95. You can also pay by phone at 866-820-5450 (the number the payment options page gives for real estate and personal property taxes), or by mail to County of Albemarle, P.O. Box 7604, Merrifield, VA 22116-7604; a payment postmarked by the due date is on time. Other options are the 24/7 kiosk at 401 McIntire Road (cash, checks and cards; 2.5% card fee), the drop boxes at the County Office Building, 401 McIntire Road, and at 1600 5th Street (the 5th Street box opens only June 1 to June 25 and November 1 to December 5; no cash in drop boxes), or in person, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. A due date that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day. Not receiving a bill does not excuse late payment. If a payment is missed, the County mails a delinquent notice 14 days after the deadline, and taxes delinquent 3 months or more go to a private collection agency, with an added fee of 20% of the amount collected.
steps.deadline: First half June 25; second half December 5
steps.fee: The tax as billed; late-payment penalty of 10 percent (at least $10), plus interest at 10% a year

steps.step: If the business closes or leaves the County after January 1, still file and pay for the whole year
steps.how: Business property tax is not prorated. A business that had property in the County on January 1 owes the full year's tax even if it closes or moves later. File the return by May 1, tick 'Business is Closed/Moved Out of Albemarle County' and give the closure date. The Existing Businesses page also says to notify the Business & Personal Tax Unit of the closure (tax@albemarle.org, or by mail to 401 McIntire Rd, Room 133). Use page 2 of the form to report a new mailing or location address.
steps.deadline: The return is still due by May 1

steps.step: Keep the records behind the return; the County audits business taxes
steps.who: Business; Business & Personal Tax Unit (business tax auditors)
steps.how: Keep the asset records that support each return. The Business & Personal Tax Unit audits business records, and also does revenue discovery and field inspections. Under state law, the County can require proper returns for the current year and the three before it, and can assess omitted taxes with penalty and interest. The return form also says a business with delinquent personal property taxes will not be issued a business license until they are paid. State law lets the Board of Supervisors require this (Va. Code § 58.1-3700(A)); the County ordinance that does so was not read.

escalation.trigger: Unsure whether property is taxable or how the business or its equipment is classified (for example, machinery and tools or not)
escalation.next: Director of Finance (Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit): a written ruling on your specific situation. Give all the relevant facts. A misrepresentation, or a change in the facts or the law, invalidates the ruling, but a taxpayer who acts on a ruling that later becomes invalid is treated as acting in good faith while it was in effect.
escalation.quote: may request a written ruling regarding the application of a local mobile property tax or a local business tax to a specific situation from the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: Assessment believed wrong, including a statutory assessment made because no return was filed
escalation.next: Director of Finance (Department of Finance & Budget): written request for correction of assessment. The County calls this the first stage of correcting an assessment, including a statutory assessment. On request, the County must give its reasons in writing. If the request is filed within 90 days of the assessment, the bill is not treated as delinquent while it is pending and for 30 days after the decision. An unpaid tangible personal property assessment can also be challenged at any time while it is collectible, with clear factual evidence that the business was not subject to the tax that year.
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A), (B); § 58.1-3981(F); § 58.1-3916; County Taxpayer Appeal Rights page
escalation.quote: within three years from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later, apply to the commissioner of the revenue or such other official who made the assessment for a correction thereof.

escalation.trigger: Disputing a business tangible personal property or machinery and tools assessment through the administrative appeal route
escalation.next: Director of Finance as assessing official: a written application for review, sent to Department of Finance & Budget, Attn: Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit, 401 McIntire Road, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902. Under state law it must identify the taxpayer, the tax period, the amount in dispute, the remedy sought, each alleged error and the grounds relied on. The County's notice also asks for the taxpayer's address, federal tax identification number and local tax account numbers, a power of attorney or letter of representation if someone else files, a copy of the assessment, and a detailed explanation. The assessment is presumed correct. The Director may hold a conference if you ask for one, and may ask for more information or an audit.
escalation.deadline: File within one year from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the assessment, whichever is later; a written determination is due within 90 days after filing
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(B)(1) to (B)(5); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of such assessment, whichever is later, to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: A timely and complete administrative appeal is pending
escalation.next: Collection of the disputed tax is suspended by the Department of Finance & Budget (as treasurer) until the final local determination, unless collection would be jeopardized by delay or the taxpayer has not answered a request for relevant information after a reasonable time (the County's notice also lists an appeal found frivolous). Interest still accrues, but no further penalty is imposed.
escalation.quote: collection activity shall be suspended by the treasurer or other official responsible for the collection of such tax until a final determination is issued by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: No final local determination after the appeal has been pending more than one year
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), after at least 30 days' written notice to the County's assessing official. The Tax Commissioner will not hear it if the delay was caused by the taxpayer's willful failure or refusal to provide information the County requested and reasonably needed.
escalation.deadline: After more than one year without a final determination, on not less than 30 days' written notice
escalation.quote: elect to treat the application as denied and appeal the assessment to the Tax Commissioner in accordance with the provisions of subsection D

escalation.trigger: The Director of Finance denies the administrative appeal in whole or in part
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner, Virginia Department of Taxation (the 2004 Guidelines give Post Office Box 1880, Richmond, Virginia 23218-1880). Serve a copy on the County's assessing official, and include a copy of the County's written determination with a statement of the facts and grounds. Collection may begin or resume after the County's final determination; it is suspended again once written notice that you intend to appeal, or the appeal itself) is filed and the County receives a copy, and that suspension ends unless the appeal is filed and served within 30 days of serving the notice. The Tax Commissioner decides within 90 days of receiving the appeal, unless the parties are told a longer period (up to 60 more days) is needed.
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the date of the County's final determination
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(D)(1), (D)(3), (E); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: may appeal the determination of the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official by filing an appeal with the Tax Commissioner and serving a copy of the appeal upon the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official within 90 days of the date of the determination

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Tax Commissioner's determination, or choosing to skip the administrative route (the County says this can be done at any point)
escalation.next: Circuit Court of Albemarle County: an application to correct the assessment, filed in the Clerk's Office. The taxpayer and the County are necessary parties, and the County Attorney defends. A direct court filing, without first using the County and Tax Commissioner appeals, does not get the state-law suspension of collection; the County's notice nonetheless says collection of the disputed portion is suspended on written notice of appeal to the court (see caveats).
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or one year from the local final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A); § 58.1-3983.1(G), (H)(5); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

escalation.trigger: Late filing or late payment penalty charged although the lateness was not the taxpayer's fault (for example death or a medically determinable impairment on the due date, lateness due solely to the County tax office, a clerical error by its staff that delayed the assessment, or proof of timely mailing)
escalation.next: Director of Finance, who performs the commissioner's and treasurer's duties in Albemarle and so decides fault for both late filing and late payment. Under the County's policy these are not grounds for a waiver: not knowing or misreading the deadline, not receiving a bill, a bill mailed to the wrong address, an incorrect bill, or wrong information from County staff.
escalation.deadline: For death or a medically determinable impairment, lack of fault is presumed if the return is filed or the tax paid within 30 days of the due date (120 days after a fiduciary qualifies, under § 58.1-3916); the County policy states the 30-day condition
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3916; County Late Payment, Filing, & Remittance Penalty Policy
escalation.quote: Penalty and interest for failure to file a return or to pay a tax shall not be imposed if such failure was not the fault of the taxpayer

escalation.trigger: An assessment is corrected after the tax was paid
escalation.next: Refund through the Department of Finance & Budget (the Director of Finance acting as treasurer). Under state law a refund of tax already paid is directed by the Board of Supervisors on the Director's certificate, with the County Attorney's consent, that the assessment was wrong; the Board may instead authorize the treasurer to approve refunds up to $10,000 (a 2022 County proposal to do so was found, but its adoption was not confirmed). Because the County charges interest on late taxes, state law requires interest at the same rate on overpayments from erroneous assessments, except on refunds of $10 or less.
escalation.quote: the governing body of the county, city or town may authorize the treasurer to approve and issue any refund up to $10,000 as a result of an erroneous assessment

escalation.trigger: A question of interpretation on a local business tax assessment that can be appealed to the Tax Commissioner, or on idle machinery and tools
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation): advisory written opinion. For idle machinery and tools, the Tax Commissioner is not required to interpret any local ordinance.
escalation.quote: issue advisory written opinions in specific cases as requested to interpret a local business tax

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

The BTPP page (2026-06-12 capture) still says '1st half 2025 BTPP taxes is due on June 25th and 2nd half is due December 5th'. The year looks stale. The dates page gives the same June 25 and December 5 dates; the 2026 form gives May 1, 2026 for the return and a late payment penalty if taxes are not paid by June 25.

Tax rate: $4.28 per $100 for tax year 2026 comes from three sources: the BTPP page, the Tax Rates page (2026-04-17 capture), and the staff report for the Board of Supervisors' April 22, 2026 adoption of the Calendar Year 2026 tax rates (Legistar file 26-256). The Board had advertised an increase to $4.43; that hearing item (file 26-240) was held on April 15, 2026. The adopted resolution itself (Attachment A) was not read. The rate is set each year.

No text of the Albemarle County Code is quoted. The County's Code of Ordinances is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access. Sections 15-101, 15-103, 15-104 and 15-800 and Chapter 15, Article 8 are cited only as County pages or Board of Supervisors agenda items describe them. Two amendments were seen only as proposals: the 2021 change moving the first-half due date to June 25 (§ 15-101), and the 2022 change omitting personal property tax under $5 (§ 15-800). Their adoption is not confirmed: Legistar records no passed date for them, though the County's pages apply the June 25 date. The County Code section that sets the return due date was not identified; the County's May 1 date matches the state default in § 58.1-3518.

Email address discrepancy: the BTPP page lists an address for emailing itemized lists on the albemarle.com domain, which is not the County's domain (albemarle.org) and is probably a typo, so it is not recorded. The 2026 form and the business tax pages give tax@albemarle.org. The older Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights (a 2023 PDF) gives a different Finance mailbox and an older fax number (434-244-4929). This page gives tax@albemarle.org and the fax number on the 2026 form, 434-243-7906.
The mailing address for returns is given as Room 133 on the County's web pages and Suite 133 on the 2026 form.

Software instructions conflict. Page 2 of the 2026 form says to include operating software 'such as Microsoft Office Products, iOS, etc.' and then says not to report Microsoft Office products. The web page lists Windows, Android, iOS and Linux as the software to report. Application software is intangible and exempt under § 58.1-1101(A)(8) and (C).

Low-value property: § 58.1-3518 lets the assessing official choose not to require a return when the property cannot generate an assessment. Albemarle instead requires every business to file every year, even with no property.
Filing extensions: § 58.1-3916 lets the Board allow extensions of up to 90 days by resolution. No Albemarle resolution or County page offering a filing extension was found.

Scope of machinery and tools differs between sources. The County lists manufacturers, miners, dairies, radio or television broadcasters, and dry cleaners or laundries, and says processors and re-processors report both classes. State law (§ 58.1-3507(A)) also covers water well drilling and advanced recycling businesses, and excludes idle machinery and tools and farm winery equipment. The County decides the classification. The Department of Taxation's idle machinery and tools guidelines (§ 58.1-3507(F)) are not covered here, nor is how capital under § 58.1-1101 is treated (§ 58.1-1101(C) exempts the listed subjects of intangible personal property).

Vehicles: highway-licensed business vehicles are not reported on this return. They are taxed as vehicle personal property, a separate process, at the same $4.28 rate per the Tax Rates page. Under § 58.1-3507(C), vehicles of machinery and tools businesses that are not DMV-registered, and their delivery equipment, are taxed as machinery and tools. How the County applies that rule was not found.

Other classes: the Board's rate notices list merchants' capital and short-term rental property among the Chapter 15, Article 8 classes. The BTPP page says daily rental property is not reported on this return; the County has a separate 1% short-term rental tax. Whether Albemarle taxes merchants' capital, and how, is not covered here.

Penalties: state law (§ 58.1-3916) would allow a late payment penalty of up to 25% on tangible personal property more than 30 days past due. The County states 10% or $10. The return form says delinquent personal property taxes block the issue of a business license. State law lets a governing body require that (§ 58.1-3700(A)), but the County ordinance adopting it was not read, because the County Code could not be read (see above).

The online portal (albemarlecountytaxes.org) is a JavaScript application, and it is not described here: whether filing the BTPP return online needs an account is not confirmed. In its business license FAQ, the Existing Businesses page says 'a new business cannot yet open an online account'; whether that also applies to filing the BTPP return is not confirmed.

Appeals: the County's appeal rights page calls a correction request the first step, and says a taxpayer can go to the Circuit Court at any point. The Tax Commissioner's 2004 Guidelines say an appeal must be pending two years before going to the Tax Commissioner for lack of a decision; the statute (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(6)) now says one year, and this page follows the statute. The Tax Commissioner's mailing address comes from those 2004 Guidelines; confirm it with Virginia Tax. The County's appeal notice addresses appeals to the 'Assessments Unit', while returns go to the Business & Personal Tax Unit.

Direct court filings: the County's Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights says collection of the disputed portion stops once written notice of a court appeal is given. Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(H)(5) says the statutory suspension does not apply to a local business tax appeal filed directly in court without first exhausting the County and Tax Commissioner appeals. Whether the County suspends collection in that case as a matter of practice should be confirmed with the Office of Revenue Administration.

Phone payments: the payment options page gives 866-820-5450 for paying real estate and personal property taxes by phone, and the Important Dates and Deadlines page lists the same number as 'General Collections' for the County's collection agency, TACS. Whether business tangible personal property bills can be paid on that line was not confirmed.

Card fees: the phone section of the payment options page lists debit cards at 2.50% and credit cards at 2.35%, the reverse of its online and in-person sections. The fees for business tax payments made through the business portal are not stated separately.

Related obligations not modelled here: the Business Audits page says a tenant listing is required each year by February 1 if you lease commercial property in the County; Va. Code § 58.1-3901(A) requires owners or operators of apartment houses, office buildings, shopping centers and similar property to file a list of tenants by February 1 when the assessing official asks. Business licenses (renewal by March 1), food and beverage tax and the short-term rental tax are separate processes.

Only office channels are recorded. Staff names on the Board of Supervisors records and a personal-looking mailbox on the Circuit Court Clerk's page were left out. The appointment-booking link contains a unit mailbox name (a role mailbox).

corrections: Quotes: all 96 draft quotes were confirmed word for word. The 67 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised), across 26 sections, and their subsection labels match the text. The 29 County and Legistar quotes were matched against Internet Archive copies of the cited albemarle.org pages and PDFs, fetched again read-only on 2026-10-11 (www.albemarle.org still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included), and against the Legistar Web API records of files 21-461, 26-240, 26-256 and 22-407. 34 quotes were added and checked the same way: 18 state-law quotes (§§ 58.1-3507(A) and (E), 58.1-3916, 58.1-3700(A), 58.1-3983.1(B)(4), (C), (D)(1), (D)(3), (E), (H)(5) and (J)(1), 58.1-3980(B) and 58.1-3981(A)) and 16 County quotes (BTPP page, Important Dates and Deadlines page, Existing Businesses page, Taxpayer Appeal Rights page and PDF, Payment Options page). The 6 short quotes inside caveats were also confirmed.
s2: added that a new business files its license application inside 30 days of starting business (Existing Businesses page), not only the March 1 renewal date.

s3: the draft left out the limits on the two small-item rules. The $25 exclusion applies only to equipment that is not machinery and tools, merchants' capital or short-term rental property, and the under-$500 aggregate estimate covers miscellaneous and incidental property (BTPP page; § 58.1-3506(A)(46), § 58.1-1101(A)(10)). Added that property used or available for use on January 1 is reported (Existing Businesses page).
s4: added the state cap on the machinery and tools rate (§ 58.1-3507(A)).

s6: 'signing a return you know is false' was narrower than § 58.1-11, which makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor to willfully subscribe a return the signer does not believe to be true and correct; reworded. The form lists the ratios and computes assessed value as (B + C) x D; 'the form applies the ratio' was reworded to say so.

s8: 'taxed as capital under § 58.1-1101, not by the County' now follows § 58.1-3507(A): idle machinery and tools are taxable as capital under § 58.1-1101, so the County does not tax them as machinery and tools. Added the return-to-use rules of § 58.1-3507(E): written notice by the next return due date without extension, tax as if in use on that year's tax day, interest regardless of fault, and no penalty with timely notice.
s9: the independent appraisal must be considered upon the taxpayer's written request and must be bona fide (§ 58.1-3507(B)); reworded from 'an appraisal you submit in writing'.

s10: the second drop box is at 1600 5th Street and opens only June 1 to 25 and November 1 to December 5 (Payment Options page); the kiosk takes cash, checks and cards with a 2.5% card fee; the phone line is given for real estate and personal property taxes; added the delinquent notice 14 days after each deadline and referral to a collection agency after 3 months (Important Dates and Deadlines page).
s11: the closure notice now cites the Existing Businesses page, which tells businesses to notify the Business & Personal Tax Unit, with its mailing address.

s12 and caveats: the draft said no state basis was found for the form's statement that delinquent taxes block a business license. Va. Code § 58.1-3700(A) lets the governing body require it; added to legal_basis. The County ordinance doing so was not read.
Escalation rung 1: added the statutory conditions of a written ruling (all facts; invalidated by misrepresentation or change; good-faith protection) (§ 58.1-3983.1(J)(1)).

Escalation rung 2: added that a correction request filed within 90 days of the assessment keeps the bill from being treated as delinquent while pending and for 30 days after (§ 58.1-3916), and the any-time challenge to an unpaid tangible personal property assessment (§ 58.1-3980(B)).

Escalation rung 3: added the full state-law contents of the appeal, the County notice's list (address, federal tax identification number, account numbers, power of attorney, copy of the assessment), and that the assessment is prima facie correct (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(2) to (B)(4)). 'A conference can be requested' now says the Director may hold one on request.
Escalation rung 4: added the two statutory exceptions to the suspension of collection (jeopardy; no response to a request for information) and the County notice's third (a frivolous appeal).
Escalation rung 5: added that the Tax Commissioner will not hear the appeal if the delay was caused by the taxpayer's willful failure to provide requested information (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(6)).

Escalation rung 6: the draft said a Notice of Intent to Appeal 'keeps collection suspended'. The County notice and the 2004 Guidelines say collection may begin or resume after the final local determination and is suspended only once the notice or appeal is filed and the County receives a copy; under § 58.1-3983.1(E) that suspension ends unless the appeal is filed and served within 30 days. Added the required contents (§ 58.1-3983.1(D)(1)) and the Tax Commissioner's 90-day determination ((D)(3)).

Escalation rung 7: added § 58.1-3983.1(H)(5) (no statutory suspension for a direct court filing without exhausting the administrative appeals), and a caveat on the County notice, which says collection of the disputed portion is suspended on written notice of appeal to the court.

Escalation rung 8: 'an error by County staff' conflicted with the County policy, which refuses waivers for erroneous information from County staff and allows them for a clerical error by the assessing staff that delayed the assessment or for lateness due solely to the tax office. Trigger and next reworded; added death as a presumptive no-fault case and the fiduciary's 120 days (§ 58.1-3916), and the other non-grounds the County lists.

Escalation rung 9: rewritten to follow § 58.1-3981(A): a refund of paid tax is directed by the Board on the Director's certificate with the County Attorney's consent, unless the Board authorizes the treasurer to approve refunds up to $10,000. Added the § 58.1-3916 rule that interest is paid on overpayments from erroneous assessments at the delinquent-tax rate (not on refunds of $10 or less).
Fees: added the 2.5% card fee at the payment kiosk and the $25 DMV stop removal fee (Payment Options and Important Dates and Deadlines pages).

Contacts: 866-820-5450 is labelled as the payment options page gives it (real estate and personal property taxes), noting that the dates page lists the same number for the County's collection agency; payments@albemarle.org is labelled as given (mortgage-company payment files and questions).
Form f4: noted the suggested Notice of Intent to Appeal (Exhibit B) in the 2004 Guidelines.
Legal basis: the § 15-101 entry now says the 2021 amendment is the proposal described in file 21-461, with adoption not confirmed, matching the § 15-800 entry.

Caveats: the 2026 form gives May 1 and June 25, not December 5 (caveat corrected); the machinery and tools scope caveat no longer says the County omits reprocessing (it lists processors and re-processors); the robots.txt caveat notes the Baiduspider and Yandex bans; the tenant-listing caveat now follows § 58.1-3901(A) (owners or operators of apartment houses, office buildings, shopping centers and similar property, by February 1 when the assessing official asks); added caveats on direct court filings, the shared phone number, the portal account FAQ and the idle machinery and tools guidelines. Sources: added §§ 58.1-3700 and 58.1-3901.

Privacy: only office channels are recorded (tax@, payments@, a unit booking mailbox, main office and fax lines, the Clerk's office line and postal addresses). The Legistar records and the Clerk's page carry staff names and a staff mailbox; none is recorded.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org blocks the research client (HTTP 403); every County page and PDF was checked only against Internet Archive copies (latest captures March to September 2026). Confirm on the live pages before relying on them.

No Albemarle County Code text was read (Municode's terms forbid automated access). Sections 15-101, 15-103, 15-104 and 15-800 and Chapter 15, Article 8 are cited as County pages and Board items describe them. The 2021 (§ 15-101) and 2022 (§ 15-800; refunds up to $10,000) amendments were seen only as proposals. The County ordinance setting the May 1 return date, any license-block ordinance under § 58.1-3700(A) and any filing-extension resolution under § 58.1-3916 were not found.

The 2026 rate resolution itself (Attachment A of file 26-256, hosted on albemarle.legistar1.com, whose robots.txt disallows all agents) was not read; the $4.28 rate rests on the staff report, the Legistar record of adoption on April 22, 2026, and the County's BTPP and Tax Rates pages.

The County notice says collection is suspended on written notice of a court appeal; § 58.1-3983.1(H)(5) withholds the statutory suspension from a direct court filing without exhausting the administrative appeals. County practice was not confirmed.

Not checked: whether online BTPP filing needs an account; whether business property bills can be paid on the 866-820-5450 line; the Tax Commissioner's current mailing address (taken from the 2004 Guidelines); the Department of Taxation's idle machinery and tools guidelines; County treatment of unregistered vehicles of machinery and tools businesses and of merchants' capital.
